rubric.why: These are the substances made during G1, and their production supports cell growth.
rubric.description: The cell makes proteins and organelles and grows.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the cell makes proteins and organelles and grows in size.

rubric.why: G1 enzymes are needed in the S phase for DNA replication.
rubric.description: The cell makes enzymes needed for DNA replication in S phase.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking enzyme production to DNA replication in S phase.

modelAnswer: During this phase cell makes proteins and organelles and so grows in size. Cell also makes enzymes that are required in S phase for the replication of DNA.

rubric.why: DNA replication is the main event and purpose of S phase.
rubric.description: The DNA of each chromosome is replicated or copied.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that DNA is copied or replicated.

rubric.why: The DNA is duplicated, but the chromosome count does not increase; each chromosome consists of two sister chromatids.
rubric.description: The chromosome number remains the same after replication.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the chromosome number stays the same.

modelAnswer: During this phase, the DNA of each chromosome is replicated (copied). It results in the duplication of chromosomes (each chromosome consists of two sister chromatids). The total number of chromosomes in cell remains the same.

rubric.why: Crossing over recombines genes, producing combinations not present in the original chromosomes.
rubric.description: Crossing over creates new combinations of genes on chromosomes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that crossing over creates new gene combinations.

rubric.why: These different combinations make the gene sets carried by gamete chromosomes unique.
rubric.description: Each chromosome in the gametes carries a unique set of genes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that gamete chromosomes carry unique gene combinations or sets.

modelAnswer: Crossing over creates new combinations of genes on chromosomes. Each chromosome in the gametes carries a unique set of genes.

rubric.why: Spindle fibres attached to chromosomes generate the movement toward the poles.
rubric.description: Spindle fibres attached to chromosomes pull them toward the poles.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that spindle fibres pull chromosomes toward the poles.

rubric.why: The pulling force separates each chromosome’s sister chromatids.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that sister chromatids separate.

modelAnswer: The spindle fibres attached with chromosomes pull toward the poles. Due to this pulling, the chromosome's sister chromatids separate.

rubric.why: In animal cells, an inward-moving furrow pinches the parent cell into two.
rubric.description: An animal cell divides by an inward-moving furrow in the cell membrane.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the animal-cell furrow moving inward or pinching the cell into two.

rubric.why: Plant cells form a plate from vesicles; it grows outward to divide the cell.
rubric.description: In plant cells, Golgi vesicles fuse to form a plate that grows outward.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the plant-cell vesicles forming a plate that grows outward.

modelAnswer: In animal cells, a furrow develops in the cell membrane at the equator. At this furrow, the cytoplasm has a ring of microfilaments. The ring contracts and the furrow moves inward. In this way parent cell is pinched into two. In plant cells, Golgi apparatus makes vesicles. These vesicles move to the middle and fuse to form a plate called phragmoplast. The plate grows outward and its membranes fuse with the cell membrane. The result is two daughter cells.

rubric.why: A chromosome is made up of two sister chromatids.
rubric.description: Each chromosome consists of two sister chromatids.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining sister chromatids as the two chromatids of a chromosome.

rubric.why: Sister chromatids separate during anaphase II and move toward opposite poles.
rubric.description: Sister chromatids separate in anaphase II.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying anaphase II as the stage when sister chromatids separate.

modelAnswer: Each chromosome consists of two sister chromatids. In anaphase-II, spindle fibres pull sister chromatids apart toward opposite poles.
